title: spent most of my weekly limit/usage to vibe code a space hauler game, any potentials?
author: Square-Yam-3772
selftext:
process: Unity3d and Codex CLI (around 1.5 weekly limit used; burned my free reset for this...)

backstory: I originally published a space hauler game around Dec 2025 but my AI-assist workflow back then was not good enough for the project so the end result was less than desirable. Last week, I came to the realization that I can rebuild it from scratch with my current process and I would get a way better result. I managed to put in the features that I originally failed to implement this time around

it is a basic space hauling game where player carries cargo across the solar system. pick up cargo, warp jumps, drop off cargo for profit. it is still very bare bone but I think I got a good foundation now.

you can find the steam link in the comment below if you are interested. 

Feel free to drop a comment if you have any questions or feedbacks. Thanks

comments.author: Aineisa
comments.body:
Cool!

Though I wonder what you will do to differentiate it from other games like the X series

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body: the game is operating at a smaller scale than the X series. Right now, it is mostly a hauler employee simulation: the player works shifts, go back to lounging and then head back out. There is no fleet or crew management etc

comments.author: jeffersonianMI
comments.body:
At a glance this seems absolutely viable.  

I would definitely dress up the UI with some skins and fonts, but it looks quite nice otherwise.  GoDot or a different engine?

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body: I just use Unity. I was around when the Unity -> Godot exodus happened but I didn't make the switch. I have been dabbling in phaser.js and three.js but I still fall back to Unity if I want to be more hands-on with the project.

comments.author: argefox
comments.body:
*SPAAAAAAACE*

NGL, I'm happy that space games are popping up. It's a hard genre, everyone goes for the arcade aspect when space flight has an incredible complexity and depth, talking about inertia dampeners bullshit, up-down alignment, etc. That's where big launches fail, they don't get space right.

I like flight sims, space sims are my jam, so my opinion is biased, but everything that has newtonian physics and decent gameplay, i'm in.

Hell, people play driving trucks, why wouldn't they play driving haulers *IN SPACE*? Add micrometeorites, good physics, engineering maintenance or random failures on thrusters vectors and nobody can say you aren't catering to the space audience. That's my honest opinion, as an old time sims, space lover and amateur dev.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body: yeah, well. I don't think I got the flight sim down either. I have had people saying that the controls are too finicky/twitchy and the physics isn't good etc. That was the last iteration so we will see if some of my old players came back to check out the current build. (the last iteration had maybe 20 unique players with a few comments...)

replies.author: argefox
replies.body: But you have to start somewhere, I mean, you have an idea, you may or may not decide to chase after it, I just provided my very biased opinion regarding space sims. It can be full arcade, but that's a genre that has been abused and saturated with small and big titles, just... I don't know, providing a niche that you could potentially exploit. Cheers.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
I did get a " its like a hamster on coffee" comment from the previous build so, haha...

at least I expose the parameters in the option this time so players can tweak the ship feels to how they like it

comments.author: ScutFarkush
comments.body: did you ever play the old EV nova games? its like the OG space hauler game. [https://escape-velocity.games/](https://escape-velocity.games/)

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body: nope but I will look into it. I actually dont know the genre very well

replies.author: CharlesDuck
replies.body: It’s not the OG. I’d say its star trader from the 70s, then we have Elite in the 80s - and then the sequel, best of them all, Frontier: Elite II from 1993

comments.author: Dresendal
comments.body: What seperates it from Star trucker?

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
the emphasis is less on trucking but it is close. 

my game doesn't force players to commit to a particular delivery. The experience is closer to a courier/trader than a trucker

Just different fantasy/vibe I suppose.

comments.author: Nervous_Teach_5596
comments.body: Well this looks will look good, do you will keep on? (And also add a way to kill that son of........ laser maker)

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body: the game has been in Early Access status for the last 6 months and this is revamp/rework #3. I probably will keep going but I haven't committed to be serious schedule yet (I was doing 1 update per month for a while and then I worked on a few other projects... I am not very disciplined)

replies.author: Nervous_Teach_5596
replies.body: Well the "cozy" but lasers shooting behind targeting you...... Maybe meteors better?

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
asteroids are in the game too. 

well, it is cozy in the sense that the shots don't have serious consequences besides losing some profits. I just want to provide some fantasy/immersion without making it about the combat.

comments.author: Jyuushiromono
comments.body:
\-The UI is too large, and it's breaking my immersion. I really need to feel like I'm actually out there in space.  
\-The spaceship's movement could use a bit more work; right now, the handling feels a little too abrupt.  
\-You could make the teleportation portal look a bit more sci-fi. The current version lowers the enjoyment of the game for me—it just feels a bit too basic.  
\-The audio... replacing the sound effects, atmospheric music, etc., with higher-quality versions would be great. Sound is one of the biggest factors in getting fully immersed in the atmosphere.

Wishing you the best of luck!

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
Hmm I am not sure what i can do with the UIs since reading the prices and the notifications are part of the gameplay. I will have to sit on that one for a bit 

I thought the audio was serviceable but I am not a sound guy so...

I am hoping the game would sell better after this revamp but we will see. Thanks

replies.author: Jyuushiromono
replies.body:
\-You could work a bit on **UX design** for the UI. Right now, it doesn't feel very intuitive or comfortable, and it breaks the overall atmosphere.  
\-Don't you have any reference games or movies that you look up to? You definitely should. It really helps you spot your shortcomings and see things you might otherwise miss.

You're very welcome, and best of luck with the development!

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
https://i.redd.it/4pqnt5x1gh8h1.gif

the UI elements are context-sensitive now i.e. sector map doesn't show until player is close to a warp gate etc. Thanks for the suggestions.

replies.author: Jyuushiromono
replies.body: Yeah, it already looks way better! You could even turn off the transparent border of that top-center indicator. Having borderless UIs over the actual gameplay screen usually makes things look much more polished. Granted, there are exceptional cases, of course.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body: good suggestion. I will just expose the panel background opacity to the options menu so players can adjust it

comments.author: Exp5000
comments.body: We need a game that blends Everspace and Stellaris/Endless Space together. I want to be the big ship with tiny ships that are completing orders and I want to manage diplomacy and trade. That's what I suggest anyhow

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body: that is a big scope. I haven't had much experience with management sim also.
